chapter_theme: Songs at Karuvur (கருவூர், also Karuvai, Garbhapuram and Vanji): pleas for Siva-jnana and for the experience of the Pati beyond pasu and pasam, a confession of the elemental body and its pride of 'I', love scenes the poet asks to leave, and a song on kings in their pomp who do not know their death, with the Mahabharata in the praise.
structure_note: Doctrinal songs (923, 925, 926), love scenes (924, 927, 929), and 928, which has no first-person plea and speaks of kings. Several Karuvur songs also name Vayali (925, 927, 928, 929).

923.reading: A short song: the poet asks to be made wise in understanding and excellent in mind, settled, and given the supreme yoga of Siva-jnana. The praise calls Murugan treasure, the eternal, his own thought, the good meaning, the refuge, the lord beyond words, at Karuvur.
923.nuance: No women and no death: the whole plea is positive, for மதி, மனம் and சிவஞான பரயோகம். சொற்பர வேளே, the lord beyond words, sets the goal past speech.

924.reading: The poet describes lovemaking: breasts like tender coconut, a pool of nectar and a pot of juice, held in both hands, the waist bending, hair slipping, lips sweet as sugar, face pressed to face, sinking into the bed, and asks to be ruled so that this deed ends. The praise names the anklets and golden shoulders with vetchi flowers that dance in the poet's eyes, Vishnu who set up the flagged chariot for Arjuna as uncle, the hunter girl's bridegroom, and the one who wounded the demon of the sea-hill, at Karuvai.
924.nuance: The plea is one phrase, சுகிக்கும் வினை அற ஆளாய், 'rule me so that the deed of enjoying ends', after a long description. நரனுக்கு அமைத்த கொடி இரதம் is Krishna as Arjuna's charioteer.

925.reading: The poet calls himself a dog who stumbles daily in the world with this body of flesh adorned from head to foot, and asks to be brought, leaving pasu and pasam, into the contemplation of the Pati, the full and partless one known by knowledge, and into that experience. The praise names Murugan son of the lord of the mountain, the rising sun of the east, master of the three Tamils and all the agamas, nectar of melting hearts, brother-in-law of Brahma, the compassionate true guru, beautiful at Karuvur in the west and at Vayali.
925.nuance: பசு பாசமும் விட்டு அறிவால் அறியப்படு பூரண நிட்கள பதி: the Siddhanta triad with its standard terms (பூரணம், நிட்களம்), ending in அநுபூதி, direct experience. கமலாலயன் மைத்துன is Brahma's brother-in-law, since Murugan's consorts are Vishnu's daughters and Brahma Vishnu's son; that reasoning is mine.

926.reading: The poet says this body of daily disease is made of earth, water, air, fire and space, yet it seeks to rule the world and win a great crown, runs about wearing ornaments and the foolish manhood that says 'I', and never sees that it is false or knows to desire true jnana; he asks to be joined by any means to Murugan's devotees and given high jnana and the life of the holy feet. The praise has drums sounding to the directions, Sura's host scattered and the serpent's hundred heads bowed by the vel, Siva who gave half his body to Shakti and burned the cities as father, and Valli's beloved, at Karuvur.
926.nuance: The body is analysed into the five elements (பிருதிவி, அப்பு, வாயு, தேயு, ககனம்) before its ambitions are listed, so the pride of rule and of 'I' (நானெனும் மடவாண்மை) rests on a heap of elements. எத்திற் கொடு நின் அடியாரொடும் உய்த்திட்டு: the means of rescue is the company of devotees. கோகுல சத்தி may call the Goddess the one of Gokula; I am unsure.

927.reading: The poet describes women whose eyes reach their earrings, breasts covered with jewelled cloth and scented with akil, embraces with nail-marks on the neck in which words stop and life faints, and asks whether, having left that experience, he will not be granted with love a disciplined contemplation. The praise names the warrior of many weapons who delights the hunters' daughter, the Kumaresa of Vayali, the vel ringed by dancing ghouls, and the six-faced lord of Garbhapuram, son of Pasupati who stands as refuge for the ruined.
927.nuance: நியமித கற்பனை is my best reading of what is asked, a regulated or ordained contemplation, but the line may divide otherwise, and விட்ட may mean the poet has left the embrace or wants to. கெர்ப்பபுரம் is Karuvur in Sanskrit, கரு = கர்ப்பம்.

928.reading: The poet pictures kings in their pomp, bowed to by ministers, princes, commanders and lesser kings, crowned with command, riding palanquin, elephant and horse under the white umbrella, fanned with whisks, proud on cotton beds, delighting in horns, flutes, songs and the dances of Konkan women, and says they do not know the death that Brahma writes. The praise tells the Mahabharata: the Pandavas lose to Sakuni's dice and go into exile, twelve years and a year in hiding, recover the cattle, are refused their share, and win the land when Krishna drives Arjuna's horses; Murugan is his nephew, Guha of Vayalur, who freed the gods, at Vanji.
928.nuance: There is no first-person plea: the whole first half describes others, and the judgment comes in one line, அயன் எழுதும் யம கோட்டியை உணராரே. The praise is apt to it, a story of a kingdom lost and won. யம கோட்டி is unclear: it may mean Yama's decree or the death written by Brahma.

929.reading: The poet describes lovemaking, hair slipping, eyes reddened, smiles, sweat, cries and lotus hands raised to the brow, and the body, a vessel of flowing sorrow, wasting in the women's embrace, and vows not to forget night and day the form in which Murugan stands at Vayali and the form at Vanji. The praise names the all-pervading lord born in Saravana for Indra's sake with six faces, the vel that pierced Krauncha, the peacock, the cock crying out against the demons, and the one who restored the gods' cities and freed them.
929.nuance: The plea does not ask to escape; it vows memory of two shrine forms, Vayali and Vanji (Karuvur), held in the heart night and day. The opening of that line (துவயலி நின்றன வ்யாத்தமும்) is garbled.

links.note: Both take kings riding elephants under the white umbrella as the case that proves death spares no one; the Naladiyar says they too were carried off, 928 that in their music and pride they never know the death Brahma has written.

923 asks to be made wise and settled and given சிவஞான பரயோகம். Tirumanthiram 2712 says that when the impurity is removed, by the power of the Lord's grace தீதில் சிவஞான யோகமே சித்திக்கும். The same compound names the goal in both, and both make it a gift of grace (அருள்வாயே, இறையருள் சத்தியால்).

After its lovemaking scene, 924 says the Lord's lotus feet with anklets and his golden shoulders with vetchi flowers dance in the poet's eyes (என் நயனத்தில் உற்று நடமிடும்). Kural 1126 has the woman say her lover does not leave her eyes (கண்ணுள்ளின் போகார்) and is not hurt when she blinks. The beloved living in the eyes is given in 924 to the god, in place of the women the song describes.

925 asks the Lord to bring the poet (அடைவித்து அருள்வாயே), leaving பசு பாசம், into the contemplation of the Pati known by knowledge. Tirumanthiram 115 says பதியினைச் சென்று அணுகா பசு பாசம், pasu and pasam cannot go to the Pati, but பதி அணுகில் they do not remain. Both make the reaching the Lord's act, not the soul's.

926 asks to be joined by any means to the Lord's devotees (எத்திற் கொடு நின் அடியாரொடும் உய்த்திட்டு) and so given high jnana and the life of the holy feet. Tirumanthiram 1644 says no tapas is needed to make the mind Siva if one has kinship (உறவு) with those whose minds have joined Siva's bliss. Both make the company of devotees the means.

927 describes the tight embrace (கட்ட முயக்கு) with nail-marks on the neck in which words stop and life faints, and asks for a disciplined contemplation having left that experience. Kural 1108 says the embrace (முயக்கு) so close that no breeze can pass between is sweet to lovers. The same close embrace is the Kural's sweetness and the Thiruppugazh's thing to be left behind.

929 vows never to forget, night and day (இராப்பகல் மறவேனே), the forms in which Murugan stands at Vayali and at Vanji. Kural 1207 has the parted woman ask what would become of her if she forgot, since she knows no forgetting (மறப்பறியேன்). The lover's vow of unbroken memory becomes the devotee's vow toward a shrine form.
